title: The Inheritance of Little Hawley
premise: Insurance investigator Bram Crane is hired to verify the death claim of Vivian Hawley, who vanished from the decaying estate of Little Hawley eleven years ago and was declared legally dead. But when Bram finds Vivian's diary in the estate's sealed attic, the entries continue past the disappearance date — written in a hand that matches Bram's own, describing events Bram has no memory of living. As Bram digs into the town's complicity in covering up what happened the night Vivian fled her powerful family, she discovers she was the child witness everyone swore didn't exist, her memory surgically buried by the same people now bankrolling the estate's sale. The diary is a message from Vivian herself, alive and hiding, forcing Bram to choose between closing the case as instructed or reopening the trial that will destroy the Hawley dynasty — and expose the price her own survival cost. In the end, Bram testifies, Vivian surrenders voluntarily, and Bram accepts that the inheritance left to her is not money but the truth.
about_author: Quentin Ishikawa is a former claims adjuster from coastal Maine whose fascination with paper trails and small-town silences informs his slow-burn mysteries. He writes under a pen name to protect the privacy of the families whose legal disputes first taught him how much truth hides inside paperwork.

chapters.title: The Claim That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Bram Crane, POV. An insurance firm hires Bram to authenticate the death-in-absentia claim on Vivian Hawley before Little Hawley estate can be sold. Bram arrives in a town that greets her with rehearsed grief. Emotional beat: professional confidence curdling into unease when the town clerk flinches at Vivian's name.

chapters.title: Eleven Winters of Dust
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Exploring the shuttered estate, Bram catalogues rooms frozen mid-life and finds the attic sealed with fresh screws despite a decade of abandonment. She pries it open and discovers a diary among preserved clothing. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by the sense of being expected.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. The diary's final dated entry falls three days after Vivian vanished — and describes watching someone examine the house, someone with Bram's habits, Bram's handwriting quirks. Emotional beat: vertigo; Bram's photographic memory confirms the script is hers, yet she never wrote it.

chapters.title: Everyone Swore
chapters.summary: Bram interviews the surviving Hawleys: patriarch Aldous, brittle and charming; his son Merritt, who handles the money. Each repeats the same polished account of Vivian's flight. Emotional beat: Bram notices their stories align too perfectly, like testimony rehearsed for a court that never convened.

chapters.title: A Memory With Seams
chapters.summary: Bram, POV, intercut with diary excerpts. Bram probes her own childhood in Little Hawley and finds a smooth, featureless year where memories should be — the year Vivian disappeared. Emotional beat: dread as she realizes her 'photographic memory' has one deliberately overexposed frame.

chapters.title: The Doctor Who Signed Nothing
chapters.summary: Bram traces the town's retired physician, Dr. Pell, who treated both Hawley daughters. He denies everything but hands her an old file 'by accident.' Emotional beat: pity curdling into anger as Bram recognizes a man who traded silence for a pension.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Divers once dragged the quarry pond for Vivian's body; the search was called off after two days by order of the county — a county Aldous Hawley funded. Emotional beat: cold clarity as Bram maps how thoroughly the machinery of power erased its tracks.

chapters.title: The Second Hand
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. A forensic document examiner confirms the post-disappearance diary entries are written by the same hand as the earlier ones — meaning either Vivian lived, or someone learned to write exactly like her. Emotional beat: hope and horror entwined; Bram wants it to be Vivian and fears what that would demand of her.

chapters.title: Merritt's Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram secretly copies Merritt's financial records and finds annual payments to Dr. Pell, the county sheriff, and a private clinic in Vermont. Emotional beat: righteous momentum — until she spots a payment line bearing her own childhood name.

chapters.title: The Clinic in Vermont
chapters.summary: Bram travels to the shuttered clinic and coaxes out a former nurse: a traumatized child was treated there for 'catastrophic memory disruption,' paid for by the Hawley family. Emotional beat: grief breaking through professionalism as Bram confronts the shape of her own erased year.

chapters.title: Sister, Witness
chapters.summary: Bram, POV, fragmented flashbacks surfacing involuntarily. Pieces return: a night, a quarrel, a fall at the quarry's edge, a small girl told to forget or be forgotten. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit — Bram survived by being unmade.

chapters.title: Aldous Invites Her to Dinner
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Aldous Hawley hosts an elegant dinner, offering Bram a generous settlement and gently reminding her that her career, her identity documents, even her name were family arrangements. Emotional beat: seduction of complicity — power doesn't threaten first; it offers comfort.

chapters.title: The Diary Writes Back
chapters.summary: Bram returns to the attic and finds a new entry in the diary, dated today: 'You remembered. Come to the boathouse alone.' Emotional beat: terror and relief colliding — Vivian is alive, watching, and has been steering Bram all along.

chapters.title: Boathouse at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Bram meets Vivian Hawley, weathered and watchful, who has spent eleven years hidden in plain sight as the estate's 'deceased' ghost, keeping the diary going to leave a trail only someone with Bram's mind could follow. Emotional beat: recognition between sisters, laced with Vivian's guilt over what forgetting cost Bram.

chapters.title: The Night at the Quarry
chapters.summary: Vivian recounts the truth: she witnessed Aldous kill their mother and stage it as an accident; fleeing, she was nearly caught, and little Bram saw everything. The family chose to erase the child rather than risk the witness. Emotional beat: catharsis and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Closing the Open Case
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. To force a trial, Bram must formally reopen the death claim — which means declaring Vivian alive, exposing her to arrest for years of identity fraud, and destroying the settlement protecting them both. Emotional beat: the investigator's creed inverted; some cases close only by being opened.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Someone tips off Merritt; the estate burns in the night, diary and evidence threatened. Bram rescues the diary from the flames as Merritt watches, understanding finally exchanged between them. Emotional beat: escalation — the family has stopped buying and started burning.

chapters.title: The Trial Begins
chapters.summary: Bram, POV, courtroom. Bram takes the stand as witness and investigator, presenting the diary, the ledger, and her own recovered memory while opposing counsel dismantles her credibility as a woman whose mind was tampered with. Emotional beat: exposure — her greatest asset, her perfect memory, becomes the thing they use to break her.

chapters.title: Vivian Walks In
chapters.summary: Climax. Against Bram's plan, Vivian surrenders herself in open court, choosing testimony over safety, corroborating every entry. Aldous's composure cracks under cross-examination as the ledger payments surface. Emotional beat: triumph earned at real cost; the sisters' truths align at last.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Aldous is convicted; Merritt settles rather than follow him down; Dr. Pell and the sheriff face charges. Bram's insurance case closes with a finding of 'life confirmed' — the strangest resolution of her career. Emotional beat: exhausted vindication, hollowed by everything it took.

chapters.title: What Survives a Fire
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Visiting the burned estate, Bram and Vivian sift the ashes and find the mother's locket, untouched. They speak plainly about the years stolen from each of them. Emotional beat: mourning without bitterness; inheritance redefined as shared truth rather than property.

chapters.title: The Next Entry
chapters.summary: Bram, POV, epilogue. Months later, Bram keeps a journal of her own now, writing forward instead of reconstructing backward. A letter arrives from Vivian, settling into her new life. Emotional beat: quiet renewal — Bram closes the case knowing some inheritances must be carried, not cashed.
